notes: Box score from the Knicks' 111–102 road win over the Toronto Raptors at Scotiabank Arena on Nov 17, 2026, from the CBS Sports box score and play-by-play, with game details from the Associated Press (via CBS Sports), The Canadian Press (via TSN), the New York Daily News and the New York Post (both via Yahoo Sports), and NY Knicks News. All 111 New York points and all 102 Toronto points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores (23–31–26–31 to 29–21–33–19) add up to both totals: 54–50 New York at the half, 83–80 Toronto after three. Team totals (rebounds 44–23, free throws 17 of 19 to 10 of 18, threes 12 of 35 to 14 of 35, field goals 41 of 78 to 39 of 78, assists 25–27, bench points 26–13) are the players' totals in the box score; The Canadian Press gives the same rebound and bench numbers. Biggest leads (Toronto 13 at 48–35 in the second quarter, New York 9 at the end) are from the play-by-play. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Tuesday's games.

Toronto led 48–35 midway through the second quarter before New York scored 19 straight and led 54–50 at the half (CBS play-by-play; The Canadian Press calls it a 19–2 run to close the half). Walter stripped Brunson and dunked with 5:04 left to put Toronto ahead 95–93 (The Canadian Press). It was tied 102–102 after RJ Barrett's layup with 1:39 left; Brunson's three off Karl-Anthony Towns's pass with 1:25 left, with Ja'Kobe Walter called for a flagrant 1, and the free throw made it 106–102, and New York closed on a 9–0 run, capped by Mikal Bridges's three with 36 seconds left (CBS play-by-play; AP; New York Daily News). Brunson scored 8 of his 31 in the fourth (The Canadian Press). Towns has a double-double in all 14 games to open the season (New York Daily News; New York Post). New York has won 15 straight against Toronto (AP; New York Daily News); the Raptors' last win in the series was Jan 22, 2023 (AP). Toronto has lost five straight (The Canadian Press). New York plays next at Minnesota on Thursday (The Canadian Press; New York Daily News).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Jalen Brunson's 3-pointer off a pass from Karl-Anthony Towns that broke a 102–102 tie with 1:25 left; Walter was called for a flagrant foul for landing-space contact and Brunson made the free throw (AP; NY Knicks News; the CBS play-by-play gives the clock and score). The stories don't say where on the arc he shot from, so it is drawn as the template's plain catch-and-shoot three. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the New York Knicks or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Jalen Brunson's listed 6-foot-2 and 190 pounds with No. 11 (RealGM), arms scaled to the 6-foot-4 wingspan measured at the 2018 draft combine (VU Hoops), in New York's road blue with his look from the look sheet. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
